question.text: How many of Taiwan's 22 mayor and county magistrate seats will the KMT win in the November 28, 2026 local elections?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the number of the 22 mayor and county magistrate races won by official KMT nominees in Taiwan's 2026 local elections, according to the [Central Election Commission](https://db.cec.gov.tw/) or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
question.fine_print:
* A winner counts for the KMT only if registered as the KMT's candidate with the CEC. TPP candidates and independents do not count, even if the KMT endorsed them.
* If a race is postponed (as Chiayi City was in 2022), the result will count if known by January 5, 2027; otherwise the race will be counted as not won by the KMT.
* Later changes of party affiliation by the winner do not affect resolution.

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46108) which opened on 2026-11-09 18:00:00.

research:
I found no result yet: the election is on 2026-11-28. Markets and commentators mostly put the KMT's likely total between about 10 and 14 of its 19 nominees.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-15: The CEC database (db.cec.gov.tw) is built by scripts and has no 2026 results yet. It says it updates within 7 days after a vote. [CEC](https://db.cec.gov.tw/)
- Count only KMT-registered nominees. The KMT has **19**: Taipei (Chiang Wan-an), New Taipei (Lee Shu-chuan), Taoyuan (Chang San-cheng), Taichung (Johnny Chiang), Tainan, Kaohsiung, Changhua, Hsinchu County, Hualien, Keelung, Kinmen, Lienchiang, Miaoli, Nantou, Penghu, Pingtung, Taitung, Yilan and Yunlin. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Taiwanese_local_elections)
- There is no KMT nominee in three races, so the maximum is 19:
  - Hsinchu City: incumbent Ann Kao is running as an independent.
  - Chiayi City: the KMT is backing the TPP's Chang Chi-kai.
  - Chiayi County: the KMT stood aside for independent Wu Pin-jui, whom it endorsed on 2026-05-26. He registered on 2026-09-03 against the DPP's Tsai Yi-yu. [CNA](https://cna.com.tw/news/aipl/202609030072.aspx), [ETtoday](https://www.ettoday.net/news/20260705/3195739.htm)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has been decided. Voting is on 2026-11-28, and no race is postponed so far.
- The KMT currently holds 14 seats, the DPP 5 and independents 3. One of the KMT's 14 is Chiayi City, which it is now ceding, so defending every seat it is contesting would mean 13 from current holdings. [China Times](https://www.chinatimes.com/realtimenews/20261113001786-260407)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-15: The KMT held Yunlin rallies for Chang Chia-chun. [UDN](https://udn.com/news/story/124652/9880390)
- 2026-11-14: KMT chair Cheng Li-wei is "cautiously optimistic" about holding Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan and Taichung (the "Defend Four" strategy). He admitted Puma Shen's "Ocean Wave" movement has energized the DPP base. [SETN](https://www.setn.com/news/1938981)
- 2026-11-14: A Shih Chien University poll in Kinmen has KMT nominee Chen Yu-jen at 45.1%, independent Lee Wen-liang at 14.8% and Chang Kuo-wei at 6.7%. Kinmen is currently held by an independent, so this is a likely KMT gain. [Newtalk](https://newtalk.tw/news/view/2026-11-14/1071141)
- 2026-11-13: Commentator Hsieh Han-ping says the KMT could lose "1-2 seats" as a floor. He calls Yilan, Changhua and Chiayi "very dangerous" and Hsinchu County high-risk. He says Taipei is a narrow lead, New Taipei is even, and the Taichung lead is smaller than expected. [China Times](https://www.chinatimes.com/realtimenews/20261113001786-260407)
- 2026-11-12: A Taipei Times columnist says polling is too thin to project seats. He calls Keelung a toss-up: Apollo has Hsieh +0.5 and Mirror has Tung +0.7. [Taipei Times](https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/feat/archives/2026/11/12/2003867584)
- Recent polls in key races, from a Wikipedia compilation (pollsters vary in reliability and lean):
  - **Taipei:**
    - Nov 10-12, New Taiwan think tank: Shen 46.3%, Chiang 42.2%
    - Nov 1-3, ETtoday: Chiang 50.7%, Shen 41.9%
  - **New Taipei:**
    - Nov 8-10: Lee 43.1%, Su 38.4%
    - Nov 1-7, UDN: Su 42%, Lee 39%
  - **Taichung:** split, with Chiang ahead in some polls and Ho in others.
  - **Taoyuan:** Chang leads.
  - **Hsinchu County:**
    - Nov 8-10, Era: Cheng (DPP) 36.9%, Hsu (KMT) 28.6%
    - Nov 5-8, Kuanchien: Hsu 44.4%, Cheng 37.5%
  - **Taitung:** Wu (KMT) leads, 35.7-43.6% against 29-31% for Chen Ying (DPP).
  - **Nantou:** Hsu (KMT) 44.6%, Wen (DPP) 30.6%.
  - **Changhua:** in October, Wei (KMT) 16% and Chen Su-yueh (DPP) 32%. The field is split.
  - **Kaohsiung:** the DPP leads by up to 7 points in the UDN poll.
  - **Yilan:** the only poll found is from August, with the DPP ahead 37.8% to 28%.

  [Wikipedia polls](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/2026%E5%B9%B4%E4%B8%AD%E8%8F%AF%E6%B0%91%E5%9C%8B%E7%9B%B4%E8%BD%84%E5%B8%82%E9%95%B7%E5%8F%8A%E7%B8%A3%E5%B8%82%E9%95%B7%E9%81%B8%E8%88%89%E6%B0%91%E6%84%8F%E8%AA%BF%E6%9F%A5)
- 2026-11-02: DPP insiders call Keelung, Yilan, Hsinchu County, Changhua and Chiayi City "breakthrough targets". They see Penghu as difficult for them. [Taipei Times](https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2026/11/02/2003867007)
- 2026-09-05: KMT internal estimate is 13-14 seats, with 4 of the 6 special municipalities. The party sees Changhua, Chiayi City and Yilan as toss-ups and a chance to take Kinmen and Penghu. The DPP's slogan is "hold 7, aim for 8, fight for 9". [World Journal](https://www.worldjournal.com/wj/story/121218/9736036)

## 4. Base rates
- KMT seats won by year:
  - 2005: 14 of 23
  - 2014: 6 of 22, under a KMT president
  - 2018: 15 of 22, under a DPP president
  - 2022: 14 of 22, under a DPP president; this included Chiayi City, decided in a postponed vote
- Midterm-style local elections usually favour the party out of the presidency, and the DPP's Lai holds it now.
- Swings between cycles can be large: from 6 seats in 2014 to 15 in 2018.
- This is not a seasonal quantity, so no calendar pattern applies.

  - YouTube host Tsai Yu-chieh: KMT 13, DPP 8, independent 1 (date unclear) [Yahoo](https://tw.news.yahoo.com/2026%E7%B8%A3%E5%B8%82%E9%95%B7%E6%9C%80%E6%96%B0%E9%A0%90%E6%B8%AC%E5%87%BA%E7%88%90-%E8%A1%97%E9%A0%AD%E6%B0%91%E8%AA%BF-3%E7%B8%A3%E5%B8%82%E8%97%8D%E5%A4%A9%E8%AE%8A%E7%B6%A0%E5%9C%B0-032703050.html)
  - A Sohu piece: KMT 14 [Sohu](https://www.sohu.com/a/1074454829_122636297)
- I found no Manifold market and no expert seat model.

## 6. Upcoming events
- Final two weeks of campaigning: the DPP is sending Lai, Hsiao and Tsai to Taipei and New Taipei, while the KMT runs its "Defend Four" push. [UDN](https://udn.com/news/story/124652/9879275)
- Taiwan's ban on publishing polls applies in the last 10 days before the vote, so no new public polls are expected after about 2026-11-18.
- The KMT-TPP friction in Hsinchu County is still a risk. KMT legislators campaigned for the TPP's Zhubei city candidate on 11-13 and 11-14, which led to "drop Wu (the KMT nominee), save Chiu (the TPP candidate)" accusations. [Newtalk](https://newtalk.tw/news/view/2026-11-14/1071147)
- Election day is 2026-11-28. A referendum on repealing the "nuclear-free homeland" policy is on the same ballot (Kalshi has it passing at 0.80). The CEC certifies results within about 7 days.
- The weather is not relevant.

I couldn't find anything that settles the count yet. Officially the KMT can win at most 19 seats. The latest polls show it safe or clearly ahead in about 9 races, with roughly 7 to 8 genuinely close.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-15: I did not fetch the CEC database (db.cec.gov.tw). It is a script-driven app, and results for 2026 won't exist until the vote on 2026-11-28. In 2022 the CEC posted 2022 results on election night.
- 2026-07-25: The KMT nominated candidates in 19 races. It stood aside in Hsinchu City and Chiayi City to back the TPP. [Focus Taiwan](https://focustaiwan.tw/politics/202607250011)
- 2026-05/09: The KMT also fielded no candidate in Chiayi County. It backs independent Wu Pin-jui (吳品叡) against the DPP's Tsai Yi-yu. Wu registered on 09-03. [CNA](https://cna.com.tw/news/aipl/202609030072.aspx)
- **The KMT can win at most 19 seats.** Wins by Kao Hung-an (independent, Hsinchu City), Chang Chi-kai (TPP, Chiayi City) or Wu Pin-jui (independent, Chiayi County) do not count. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Taiwanese_local_elections)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing is settled. The vote is on 2026-11-28. Under Taiwan's election law, new polls cannot be published in the last 10 days before the vote, from about 11-18.

## 4. Base rates
- KMT seats won by year:
  - 2014: 6 of 22.
  - 2018: 15 of 22.
  - 2022: 14 of 22. This was 13 on election night plus Chiayi City, which voted on 12-18 after the race was postponed. [Wikipedia 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Taiwanese_local_elections)
- Seat counts have swung by up to about 9 between elections (6 to 15). Late polls have often missed by several points in individual races.
- The ceiling of 19 nominees is higher than in 2022. But three races (Hsinchu City, Chiayi City and Chiayi County) are off the table for the KMT whatever happens.
- This is not seasonal, so a seasonal comparison doesn't apply.

## 5. Other forecasts
Prices as fetched on 2026-11-15:
- **Polymarket, KMT seat count:** ≤7: 9%, 8: 18%, 9: 32.5%, 10: 41%, 11: 19.5%, 12: 16.5%. These add up to about 129%, so the market looks thin or the prices are stale midpoints. No buckets above 12 were listed. The mode is around 9 to 10, well below the 14 the KMT now holds.
- **Polymarket, party winning most local races:** KMT 66.5%, DPP 34.5%.
- **Polymarket, "Mayoral Elections" party winner:** KMT 36%, DPP 62%. This may cover only the six special municipalities; check the market's rules.
- **Kalshi, local elections overall winner:** KMT 65%.
- **Kalshi, Taipei:** Chiang (KMT) 65%, Shen (DPP) 35%.
- **Kalshi, Hsinchu County:** Cheng (DPP) 70%, Hsu (KMT) 29%.
- **Polymarket, Hsinchu combo:** "Kao + Cheng" (Kao winning Hsinchu City, Cheng winning Hsinchu County) is at 50.5%.
- **Taiwan Public Opinion Index (台灣民心指數), October:** asked which party will win a majority of races, 38.1% said the DPP and 28.7% the KMT. [China Times](https://www.chinatimes.com/realtimenews/20261027001614-260407)
- I found no Metaculus community figure.

Rough reading of the races from the sources above:
- **KMT clearly ahead (about 9):** Taoyuan, Nantou, Kinmen, Lienchiang, Taitung, Hualien, Miaoli, Yunlin, Penghu. Polls in the last four are thin or old.
- **Close (about 7 to 8):** Taipei, New Taipei, Taichung, Keelung, Hsinchu County, Kaohsiung, and possibly Yilan.
- **DPP favoured:** Tainan, Changhua, Pingtung.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-11-18: the 10-day ban on publishing polls begins, so no new public polls after that.
- 2026-11-28: election day, also with a referendum on repealing the nuclear-free homeland policy. Results are expected the same night.
- 2026-11-14 and after: final rallies, KMT-TPP joint events and DPP presidential-level campaigning in Taipei and New Taipei. Friction between the KMT and TPP, such as the Zhubei controversy where KMT legislators campaigned for the TPP candidate over the KMT's own, could hurt KMT turnout in Hsinchu County.
- A postponement, as happened in Chiayi City in 2022, would only matter if the result came after 2027-01-05.
- Weather: not relevant.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 13 days remain until the November 28 vote. Results are known election night, and CEC certification follows within about a week, before resolution around December 1.

(b) There are no 2026 results yet. The latest relevant baseline is the KMT's 14 seats from 2022 (as of 2026-11-15). Of those, 13 are races it is contesting this year, because it ceded Chiayi City. It has 19 nominees in total, so 19 is the maximum.

(c) If every current holder kept their seat, the KMT would get 13. Adding Kinmen, where its nominee leads strongly, gives 14.

(d) Recent trends have moved against the KMT:
- Puma Shen's movement has energized the DPP base.
- Taipei and New Taipei are tightening.
- The DPP leads in Changhua and Yilan.
- Kalshi favours the DPP in Hsinchu County.
- Keelung is a toss-up.

My race-by-race probabilities add up to an expected total of about 10.7. The safest seats are Lienchiang, Hualien, Taoyuan, Miaoli, Nantou, Taitung and Kinmen. The coin-flips are New Taipei, Taichung, Keelung and Penghu. The KMT is an underdog in Yilan, Hsinchu County and Changhua, and a long shot in Kaohsiung, Tainan and Pingtung.

(e) The KMT total can swing a lot between cycles: from 6 seats in 2014 to 15 in 2018. Within the last two weeks of a campaign, though, uncertainty is mostly about correlated polling error across races, roughly plus or minus 2 to 3 seats.

(f) Experts and markets disagree:
- The KMT's internal estimate is 13 to 14. Commentators say 13 to 14, but they are often partisan.
- Polymarket's seat buckets are noisy, with mass at 9 to 10 and again at 13 to 14.
- Kalshi gives Chiang 0.65 in Taipei and the KMT 0.29 in Hsinchu County.
- The KMT is about 0.65 to win the most races.

(g) Low scenario: a late DPP surge nationally, helped by the "Ocean Wave" mobilization and KMT-TPP friction, costs the KMT Taipei, New Taipei, Taichung, Keelung, Yilan, Changhua, Hsinchu County and Penghu. That leaves about 7 or 8 seats.
High scenario: a midterm penalty for President Lai plus high blue turnout lets the KMT sweep all the toss-ups and win Kinmen and Penghu. That gives 15 or 16 seats.

(a) Time left: 13 days until the November 28, 2026 vote. CEC results should follow within about 7 days, well before resolution around December 1 to 5.

(b) Latest known value: There are no 2026 results yet (CEC, as of 2026-11-15). The KMT currently holds 14 seats. One of these, Chiayi City, is being ceded to the TPP, and the KMT has nominees in only 19 races, so 19 is the hard maximum.

(c) If nothing changed: Holding every contested seat it now has would give 13. Gaining Kinmen on current polling would make it about 14. That is the ceiling of a status-quo outcome, not the expectation, because several holdings are at risk.
